messages:
Sam: Ran an end-to-end profiling pass on mixtral-7b-8k serving stack yesterday evening. Seeing a 2.3x tail-latency spike when RoPE scale is set to 1.2 and tokenization triggers byte-fallback.
Maya: dump the flamegraph? link?
Sam: https://dash.internal/perf/trace/abc123 (redwood perf dashboard) — flame shows a hot path in kernel_selector -> fallback_byte_kernel -> kv_cache_miss_handler. pprof snippet:
```
flat  flat%   sum%   cum   cum%
200ms 45.3% 45.3% 300ms 68.0% kernel_selector::select_kernel
80ms  18.1% 63.4% 120ms 27.2% kv_cache::get_or_evict
50ms  11.3% 74.7% 50ms  11.3% tokenizer::byte_fallback
```
Carlos: interesting — is byte-fallback happening for many requests or a small tail? Could be chat template with system + user causing >512 token prelude that triggers fallback.
Sam: Roughly 9% of requests in the trace hit byte-fallback. They correlate to chat prompts with long system messages + code blocks (we saw many 3-4k token counts). KV cache miss rate for those requests ~32% vs baseline 5%.
Jen: That suggests cache key variance due to dynamic system msg: maybe we don't normalize chat template whitespace or special tokens. Any example prompt?
Sam: Example:
`[SYSTEM] You are a helpful assistant.\nUser: <user_message>\n### CONTEXT:\n<large_context_blob>`
Some customers include timestamps inside system or ephemeral IDs which breaks prefix matching and KV reuse.
Maya: Two levers here: 1) prevent byte-fallback by pre-tokenizing and forcing utf8-safe path (we already have detect-and-escape in tokenizer shim), 2) reduce kernel-selector's eagerness to fall back — pick quantized kernel only after checking kv_cache hit probability.
Carlos: For #2 we could add a cheap heuristic: if seq_len_prefetch > kv_cache_window or first_n_tokens have nonzero special-token rate -> avoid byte kernel. Bench it.
runtime-oncall: FYI perf-bot alerted at 01:13UTC: deploy 2026-03-14. No rollback yet.
perf-bot: [ALERT] mixtral-7b-8k tail latency +110% over baseline for 30m. Spike correlates with new chatfmt template rollout.
Jen: Another angle: batching heuristics. Our batcher currently sets batch_size cap 32 and batch_age_ms 8ms. Large variance in token counts means some batches get starved waiting for slow byte-fallback streams, increasing p50 for others.
Sam: Yeah saw that — reordering helps: prefer groups with similar token-length estimate. We could add a length-homogenous binning step (fast O(1) bucketing) before batching.
Maya: Should also bump kv cache warmup: when a conversation resumes after a gap we warmup by preloading last 8 keys — but for huge system messages the prefix isn't useful. Maybe restrict warmup to last N tokens excluding system block.
Carlos: Model-specific note: Mixtral RoPE scaling >1.0 interacts poorly with kernel heuristics on our CUDA kernels; some kernels assume linear RoPE scale and get extra compute in matmul layout. We should add a kernel flag 'ropecalc_mode' and route Mixtral->special-rope-kernel when scale !=1.0.
Sam: Agreed. I can prototype kernel selector patch: prefer rope-aware kernel if model.meta.rope_scale != 1.0 or if head_dim%64 != 0. Also add unit tests for kv cache invariants.
Jen: Action items: 
- Sam: prototype kernel selector patch + microbench (deadline EOD Thu)
- Maya: add quick tokenizer pre-pass to detect and avoid byte-fallback for chat templates (EOD Fri)
- Carlos: run end-to-end A/B with length-binning batcher in staging, compare tail latency and cost (mid-next-week)
- runtime-oncall: add alert rule for byte-fallback rate > 5% per-queue

Sam: I'll post the PR link once green. For now we can rollout a canary with kernel selector guarded by a flag.
Maya: +1. Also logging: add normalized-system-hash to trace for easier debugging (no PII).
Carlos: Will add perf traces to the canary run.
Jen: Thanks — seems like a small set of changes to get latency back without model changes. :thumbsup:
runtime-oncall: tagging @oncall to watch the canary.
Sam: Uploading the pprof tarball here: /mnt/artifacts/mixtral_rope_pprof.tar.gz
Maya: ack, will pick this up after standup.
